units.text: It reads and writes PDF documents, extracts text from pages, and creates or modifies form fields and annotations. It supports reading PDF files to access embedded images and writing new PDF files with text fragments, form fields, and widget annotations. It operates on Java 11.
It creates new PDF documents and edits existing ones by adding pages, text fragments, and annotations using the Document, Page, and TextFragment classes.
It extracts text using TextAbsorber and images as XImage objects from specific pages, saving them to external files.
It works with forms and annotations by creating and manipulating widget annotations, radio button option fields, and form fields such as text boxes through the Document and Form APIs.
It renders PDF pages to raster images using device classes and extracts plain text per page with TextDevice.
It secures and optimizes documents by encrypting with AES or RC4 and optimizing resources through Document.optimizeResources.
It manages document structure by building and inspecting the logical structure tree rooted at StructTreeRoot and working with tagged PDF content.
This example creates a new PDF document, adds a page, and inserts a widget annotation with a red border, then prints the RGB values of the border color to the console.

The following workflows demonstrate common tasks with Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java, including mixing text and form fields in table cells, extracting text, extracting images, creating PDFs from scratch, and reading or updating form fields.
Mix plain text and a radio button option field in a table cell.
Extract text from an existing PDF document.
Extract images from a specific page in a PDF.
Create and save a new PDF with a text fragment.
Read and update form fields in an existing AcroForm.
Insert multiple radio button option fields in a cell.
Set and retrieve the background color of a widget annotation.
Configure and inspect the border style of a radio button option field.

Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java exposes the Document class as its central entry point for working with PDF documents, with page access provided through PageCollection and Page types. Convenience operations for editing, extracting, converting, and signing PDFs are available via dedicated facade classes.
The org namespace serves as the root package for the Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java library, under which all public API types are organized.
The org.aspose namespace contains core API types shared across Aspose products, including base classes and common interfaces used by the PDF module.

The org.aspose.pdf namespace hosts the main PDF-specific classes such as Document, Page, PageCollection, and the facades PdfFileEditor, PdfContentEditor, PdfBookmarkEditor, PdfExtractor, PdfConverter, and PdfFileSignature.

Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java is a Java library for working with PDF documents.

OCR, conversion to non-PDF formats other than HTML/XML, conversion from non-PDF formats other than HTML, full XFA form rendering, and 3D annotations and PRC/U3D streams are not supported; the Maven install command is mvn dependency:get -Dartifact=org.aspose:aspose-pdf-foss:26.9.0.

Partially implemented today: PdfFileSecurity.setAllowExceptions throws UnsupportedOperationException, text replacement with non-Latin scripts may differ from a reference renderer, resource optimization is limited, tagged PDF support is partial, PDF/X validation and conversion lacks dedicated test coverage, and public-key-encrypted PDFs require a custom security handler.
A single Document instance is not thread-safe — use one Document per thread, opening separate instances for parallel processing.

Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java targets Java 11+ and builds with Maven 3. Tests use JUnit 5 (Jupiter) and build any PDF fixtures in-memory or via @TempDir, so the repository ships no sample PDF corpus. CI runs on every push via .github/workflows/build.yml and releases publish to Maven Central via .github/workflows/maven-central-release.yml.
It adds broader format conversion (including OCR and non-PDF output formats), full feature completeness, and commercial support.
LoadFormat represents the format of a PDF document being loaded.
DoWhileStmt represents a do-while statement in the JavaScript AST.
XfaPacket represents an XFA packet with properties such as name, source bytes, and dirty state.
